name: Waalaxy
tagline: Manage a manual relationship workflow without automating protected-platform actions

pricing.notes: Typical public Pro amount; regional currency and platform-policy changes require recheck.

tiers.name: Pro
tiers.limits: 300 LinkedIn invites/month, unlimited campaigns, pre-built sequences, automated follow-ups, CRM sync, 25 email finder credits/month.
tiers.notes: Published at €19/user/month monthly; converted at about 1 EUR = 1.155 USD; annual shown as -50%.

tiers.name: Advanced
tiers.limits: 800 LinkedIn invites/month, unlimited campaigns, API access, Make/Zapier/n8n modules, live chat support, 25 email finder credits/month.
tiers.notes: Published at €49/user/month monthly; converted at about 1 EUR = 1.155 USD; annual shown as -50%.

tiers.name: Business
tiers.limits: 800 LinkedIn invites/month, cold email sequences, multichannel campaigns, multiple sender accounts, 500 email finder credits/month.
tiers.notes: Published at €69/user/month monthly; converted at about 1 EUR = 1.155 USD; annual shown as -50%.

pricing.freeTierCaps: no free tier; 14-day free trial on paid plans.
pricing.billingTerms: monthly, quarterly (-20%) and yearly (-50%); prices published in EUR and converted to USD
pricing.hiddenCosts: Email finder credits are capped at 25/month on Pro/Advanced and 500/month on Business; annual USD values are converted from stated EUR monthly price with stated yearly discount.

verdictSummary: A consolation build is possible, but the paid product's decisive value sits outside a solo rebuild. For Waalaxy, manage a manual relationship workflow without automating protected-platform actions. The hard boundary is linkedin-dependent automation, enrichment, templates, and established workflow, plus proprietary data, deliverability, and network effects.
coreLoopDIY: Import a permissioned lead list, personalize a modest manual outreach sequence, enforce sending limits, and track replies without automating protected-platform actions or supplying proprietary contact data.
whatYouLose: LinkedIn-dependent automation, enrichment, templates, and established workflow
moatNotes: proprietary data, deliverability, and network effects
ongoingBurden: consent records, suppression lists, DNS, bounces, reputation, abuse complaints, provider limits, and changing email rules
whyPeopleStillPay: People still pay for Waalaxy because the durable value is accurate contact data and deliverability infrastructure; a sequence editor alone is not the product. The recurring cost buys consent records, suppression lists, DNS, bounces, reputation, abuse complaints, provider limits, and changing email rules, not just the visible interface.

priorArt.name: Mautic
priorArt.desc: Open-source marketing automation platform with campaigns, contacts, and email workflows.

alternatives.name: EspoCRM
alternatives.desc: A traditional CRM that actually lets you change the data model; polished enough, but still your server.

facts.install: Docker Compose or upload the PHP package and run the web installer
facts.dataFormat: CRM records in a self-hosted MySQL, MariaDB, or PostgreSQL database; uploaded files in server/Docker volumes
facts.gapVsPaid: EspoCRM can track relationships manually but does not automate LinkedIn actions or coordinated LinkedIn-and-email sequences as Waalaxy does.
facts.setupBlocker: Requires a server, database, domain/TLS setup, and ongoing upgrades/backups

alternatives.name: Frappe CRM
alternatives.desc: A clean leads-and-deals board with notes, tasks and email; Frappe underneath means a real server, not a toy.

facts.install: One-click Frappe Cloud signup or the official Python easy-install deployment script on your server
facts.dataFormat: CRM DocType records and attachments in the Frappe site database/files, on Frappe Cloud or the user's server
facts.gapVsPaid: Frappe CRM records leads and follow-ups but provides no Waalaxy-style LinkedIn prospecting automation or multichannel sequences.
facts.setupBlocker: Free use means self-hosting; the official production script still needs a Linux server, DNS, and command-line access

alternatives.name: HubSpot Free CRM
alternatives.desc: A real two-seat CRM for free; 1,000 contacts is where the upsell starts counting.

facts.install: Hosted signup; optionally connect/import email, calendar, and contacts
facts.dataFormat: Structured CRM customer records stored and processed on HubSpot's cloud servers, with regional hosting options and exports
facts.gapVsPaid: HubSpot Free can store prospects but does not reproduce Waalaxy’s automated LinkedIn visits, connection requests, messages, and follow-up sequences.

alternatives.name: Krayin CRM
alternatives.desc: A Laravel sales pipeline with leads, contacts and email; glossy enough, but it still wants a PHP stack.

facts.install: Composer package, browser GUI installer, or Docker; managed cloud is also offered
facts.dataFormat: CRM records in MySQL/MariaDB (Laravel database); uploads in storage/app/public on the chosen host
facts.gapVsPaid: Krayin provides a pipeline but no Waalaxy-style LinkedIn automation or multichannel campaign engine.
facts.setupBlocker: The free path requires PHP/Composer plus MySQL/MariaDB, or Docker and a server; HTTPS, backups, and updates remain yours

alternatives.name: Twenty
alternatives.desc: A modern pipeline CRM with custom objects, views and mailbox sync; the subscription becomes a Compose file.

facts.install: Hosted cloud signup or official one-line/Docker Compose self-host install
facts.dataFormat: CRM records and configuration in PostgreSQL; files in local storage or S3-compatible object storage on the selected host
facts.gapVsPaid: Twenty handles contacts and mailbox sync but leaves Waalaxy’s LinkedIn prospecting and multistep outreach entirely manual.
facts.setupBlocker: Free use requires Docker, at least 2 GB RAM, PostgreSQL-backed containers, secrets, and domain/TLS configuration

alternatives.name: Monica
alternatives.desc: A self-hosted relationship memory for people, notes, reminders, and follow-ups; LinkedIn stays manual.

facts.install: Hosted signup or Docker Compose with the official Monica image and MariaDB
facts.dataFormat: Contacts, notes, reminders, and relationships in MySQL/MariaDB; uploaded files in a persistent storage volume, or on Monica's hosted servers
facts.gapVsPaid: Monica remembers people and follow-ups but has neither a sales campaign engine nor any LinkedIn automation.
facts.setupBlocker: The unrestricted free path needs Docker, a database, an application key, persistent volumes, and a reverse proxy/TLS for public use

alternatives.name: Odoo CRM One App Free
alternatives.desc: A hosted contact-and-follow-up workflow for unlimited users; no LinkedIn robot in sight.

facts.install: Hosted Odoo Online signup with CRM selected as the single free app
facts.dataFormat: Structured Odoo records in an Odoo-hosted customer database; records can be exported from list views
facts.gapVsPaid: Odoo can schedule follow-ups but does not automate the protected-platform actions and multichannel sequences Waalaxy sells.

notes: Editorial comparison targets the Pro plan and a small permission-based outreach console DIY substitute. Recheck price before merge.
prompt:
Build a closest honest personal substitute for Waalaxy in an empty repository.
Use Next.js 15, TypeScript, PostgreSQL, Drizzle ORM, and a user-chosen transactional email provider; do not offer alternative stacks.
The core loop is: import a permissioned lead list, personalize a modest manual outreach sequence, enforce sending limits, and track replies without automating protected-platform actions or supplying proprietary contact data.
Make the first run work locally with one documented command.
Store all user data locally by default and make export straightforward.
Put secrets in .env, ship .env.example, and never commit credentials.
Accept CSV imports only after the user confirms lawful collection and records the source.
Provide contact fields, tags, suppression status, consent notes, and a complete change history.
Build a short email sequence with delays, business-hour windows, and per-domain rate limits.
Use the configured provider for sends and process delivery, bounce, complaint, and unsubscribe webhooks.
Stop sequences immediately on reply, bounce, complaint, suppression, or manual pause.
Show deliverability warnings, daily send totals, and a mandatory preview before activation.
Include clear empty, loading, success, and recoverable error states.
Add input validation, safe filenames, and graceful handling of unavailable APIs.
Write focused tests for the core transformation and one end-to-end happy path.
Create a README with setup, architecture, permissions, data location, and backup steps.
Do not add accounts, billing, telemetry, analytics, or a hosted control plane.
Do not claim to reproduce proprietary data, network liquidity, regulated access, or frontier infrastructure.
Deliberately leave out scraping protected platforms.
Deliberately leave out buying or generating personal contact data.
Deliberately leave out automated inbox warm-up networks and evasion of provider limits.
Finish by running the tests and listing the exact commands used.
